Because OP didn't sauce all 4 EOs and Voat's dysfunctional website won't let me post links, here is the short version:

1) Making insulin and Epipens available to patients at 340B prices for certain low-income individuals.

2) Allowing drugs to be imported by: allowing grants to allow import of certain drugs currently prohibited from importation, allowing insulin to be imported, allowing certain prescription drugs to be imported from Canada.

3) Attacking PBMs by: making PBMs subject to anti-kickback statutes (but with a lot of legal mumbo jumbo that basically means they don't understand how the PBMs add value to the supply chain and why their business model works).

4) Pegging Medicare Part D drug purchase price to prices offered to a designated Most Favored Nation.

Like all EOs, these aren't laws. They're only modifications of how laws already on the books are enforced. Their impacts are all, therefore, really limited. Making insulin and Epipens available through this back channel is going to be a logistical nightmare for patients and the pharmacists or social workers trying to get them signed up, and it doesn't specify how poor you have to be to qualify (details, right?). None of the companies that doubled the price of insulin in only 4 years are going to drop their list price one penny. The government is going to buy insulin for a handful of people who likely already qualify for Medicaid anyway.

Allowing importation of drugs from Canada falls into the same category. 1) We don't know which drugs. 2) There's likely going to be a caveat that the drugs be manufactured according to CGMP standards required by the FDA, sharply limiting which drugs can be imported - again, because EOs can't rewrite the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, they can only modify it's enforcement. We'll have to see how much opens up and how industry reroutes their supply chains.

The PBM thing is a double-edged sword. PBMs are like octopi with their tentacles on nearly every aspect of the pharmacy supply chain. What they do is legal. They buy in massive bulk from manufacturers, which is why they get the rebates. They resell those drugs to individual pharmacies below the list price and keep some of the rebate for their trouble. Trump's arguing their entire business model is unethical. It's not. They create economies of scale, which is why they exist, as much our gut reaction is to hate the fact that they're profiting off of sick people. Ultimately, they're going to find few opportunities to successfully sue anyone depending on how they open up the anti-kickback statute (again, details matter and Trump doesn't provide them). But, here's the other edge of the sword, if they do successfully get sued, they're not going away. Drug prices will end up going higher as they shift their legal costs onto pharmacies and 3rd party payers, who'll then bill patients higher prices.

The last one is the only one that stands much chance, and it's another double edged sword. Medicare and Medicaid buy ~50% of all drugs in the US. Most insurers peg their coverage to Medicare rates. If Medicare starts dropping their prices by pegging them to Guatemala (or whatever country), manufacturers still need to cover their costs. And it's not just manufacturing. The biggest costs to pharma companies after payroll are research, clinical trials, and discounts to low-income patients. They're not going to cut payroll and they're sure as hell not going to stop discounts to low-income patients. It'd be a PR nightmare. What they will do is cut back on their research, especially on anything that takes time or has a low ROI (orphan drugs, antibiotics, etc). Anything new is going to be priced high enough to bankrupt a 3rd-world dictator. US pharma companies do ~90% of the research worldwide. We're about to slash DEEP into that for a short-term gain.

PORTLAND, Ore.—U.S. Attorney Billy J. Williams announced today that 18 people have been arrested and are facing federal charges this week for their roles in recent weeknight protests at the Mark O. Hatfield U.S. Courthouse in Portland.

According to court documents, since May 26, 2020, protests in downtown Portland have been followed by nightly criminal activity including assaults on law enforcement officers, destruction of property, looting, arson, and vandalism. The Hatfield Federal Courthouse has been a nightly target of vandalism during evening protests and riots, sustaining extensive damage.

U.S. Marshals Service deputies and officers from the Federal Protective Service, Homeland Security Investigations, and U.S. Customs and Border Protection working to protect the courthouse have been subjected to nightly threats and assaults from demonstrators while performing their duties.

Five people have been charged for alleged criminal conduct during a protest beginning July 20, 2020 and continuing into the early morning hours of July 21, 2020. Jennifer Kristiansen, 37, is charged with assaulting a federal officer; Zachary Duffly, 45, is charged with creating a disturbance; Wyatt Ash-Milby, 18, is charged with trespassing on federal property; and Caleb Ehlers, 23, and Paul Furst, 22, are charged with failing to comply with a lawful order.

Seven people have been charged for alleged criminal conduct during a protest beginning July 21, 2020 and continuing into the early morning hours of July 22, 2020. Jerusalem Callahan, 24, is charged with willfully damaging government property; Joseph Ybarra, 21, is charged with arson; Marnie Sager, 27, and Ella Miller, 26, are charged failing to comply with a lawful order; and Taylor Lemons, 31; Giovanni Bondurant, 19; and Gabriel Houston, 22, are charged with assaulting federal officers.

Six people have been charged for alleged criminal conduct during a protest beginning July 22, 2020 and continuing into the early morning hours of July 23, 2020. Joseph Lagalo, 37; Baily Dreibelbis, 22; Nicholas Kloiber, 26; David Hazan, 24; Hailey Holden, 30; and Cameron Knuetson, age unknown, are charged with failing to comply with a lawful order.

All defendants are presumed to be local residents.

All 18 defendants have made their first appearances in federal court and were ordered released pending jury trials or other follow-up court proceedings.

These cases are being jointly investigated the U.S. Marshals Service and Federal Protective Service. They are being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Oregon.
